findings.title: The validator's answer for a command key recorded unknown, and for a leading word no key matches, is unstated
findings.recommendation: State both outcomes in the validator paragraph and design D5: a key the contract records with known: false fails with git's recorded line (`is not a git command` / `unknown subcommand`); a leading word that matches no recorded key — a subcommand a body gained after capture — fails as `unknown command "<x>" for "git"` with the re-capture hint, as an unrecorded flag does. Task 3.1 and D6's unknown-subcommand injection assert the message, so the two paths need one written answer each.
findings.reproduction: Constructed case: the surface carries `git frobnicate <path>` at capture time, so the contract holds `"frobnicate": {known: false, message: "git: 'frobnicate' is not a git command..."}`. The validator paragraph says only "look up the longest command key leading the argument vector"; the lookup succeeds on a key whose entry says unknown, and nothing says whether it fails with that message, with D5's `unknown command` string, or proceeds to check flags against an empty flag list. A second implementer meeting a post-capture `git rebase <x>` (no key at all) has D5's string but no re-capture hint, unlike the unrecorded-flag path.

findings.title: A group's verb is not required to be a word, as the prototype required
findings.recommendation: Add to the command-key row: a group's verb is the segment's second token only when it matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`; a group segment whose second token is a flag or a placeholder has no key and fails as an unknown command. The prototype applied exactly this test (explore.md Case 2); the spec row dropped it.

walk_entry.title: No rule decides whether a git segment's second word is a subcommand (worktree remove) or a positional (push <remote>)

findings.title: explore.md changed after the pair and is in no walk entry's edit record
findings.recommendation: Record gap only: the re-exploration (D-rc05b-9 to D-rc05b-12, Cases 1–3) edited explore.md on the redesign route, which is the route the walk named; no defect found in it. Nothing to change unless a later walk wants the route's edits listed.

commentary: Graded each resolved entry over its sweep scope against the files as they stand. The redesigned probe table matches the prototype the re-exploration executed row for row, with one loss: the prototype only took a word as a group's verb, and the spec's key row does not say so. The descoped =value limit, the grouping row, the inline gate and the non-goal all landed where their entries say and nowhere contradicts them; the old probe wording survives only in explore.md and the trail. The one new gap sits in the validator, outside every walk: it was written before the capture recorded unknown keys, and the two kinds of unknown command now need their own answers.

D3's `=value` rule cannot be implemented from D3's own contract shape, and the validator says nothing about `=value` on a no-value flag
